title: Isolation and Functional Analysis of Peridroplet Mitochondria from Murine Brown Adipose Tissue
author: Ngo, Benador, et al.

steps.title: Prepare all buffers and aliquots
steps.instruction: Prepare batches of Mitochondrial Isolation Buffer (MIB), Mitochondrial Assay Solution (MAS), and all respirometry substrate solutions. Store each buffer in single‑use aliquots at –20 °C for up to 6 months. For MAS + GDP without substrates, aliquot 20 mL per 96‑well plate; for 10× substrate buffers with ADP aliquot 1.5 mL per plate, and without ADP aliquot 2 mL per plate.

steps.title: Adjust MAS pH after substrates
steps.instruction: After adding respirometry substrates (e.g., pyruvate and malate) to MAS, measure the pH and adjust it to exactly 7.2 because pH ≤ 6 inhibits mitochondrial respiration.

steps.title: Prepare MIB with/without BSA
steps.instruction: Make two MIB stocks: one containing bovine serum albumin (BSA) to bind free fatty acids released during homogenization, and one without BSA for the final resuspension of the mitochondrial pellet (BSA interferes with downstream protein quantification).

steps.title: Pre‑cool all reagents and equipment
steps.instruction: Place all solutions, tubes, centrifuge rotors, homogenizer, and other equipment on ice or in a 4 °C environment and keep them ice‑cold throughout the isolation to preserve mitochondrial integrity.

steps.title: Dissect and keep BAT on ice
steps.instruction: Harvest brown adipose tissue (BAT) from mice, immediately place the tissue on ice, and proceed to homogenization.

steps.title: Homogenize BAT in cold MIB
steps.instruction: Transfer the BAT into cold MIB containing BSA and homogenize with a glass‑Teflon Dounce homogenizer until a uniform suspension is obtained.

steps.title: Low‑speed centrifugation to separate fractions
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at low speed (temperature 4 °C; speed and time as per Materials table) to generate a floating fat layer (fraction 1, peridroplet mitochondria, PDMs) and a clear supernatant (fraction 2, cytoplasmic mitochondria, CMs).

steps.title: Collect fat layer and supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate the floating fat layer (fraction 1) into a separate tube and collect the supernatant (fraction 2) into another tube, keeping both on ice.

steps.title: High‑speed centrifugation of each fraction
steps.instruction: Subject each fraction to high‑speed centrifugation at 4 °C (speed and time as per Materials table). This step pellets PDMs after stripping them from lipid droplets in fraction 1 and pellets CMs from fraction 2.

steps.title: Resuspend mitochondrial pellets
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatants and gently resuspend each mitochondrial pellet in MIB **without** BSA (the BSA‑free buffer prepared in step 3). Keep the suspensions on ice.

steps.title: Hydrate Seahorse sensor cartridge
steps.instruction: Place the Agilent Seahorse XF96 sensor cartridge in the hydration buffer and hydrate for at least 4 hours before the assay.

steps.title: Create Seahorse assay template
steps.instruction: In the XF96 Analyzer software, create a new assay template that matches the protocol described below, then save the template before loading samples.

steps.title: Load mitochondria into XF96 plate
steps.instruction: Dispense the appropriate volume of each mitochondrial suspension into the wells of a Seahorse XF96 plate (adjust mitochondrial protein amount if using equipment other than Seahorse).

steps.title: Run Seahorse respirometry protocol
steps.instruction: Execute the following timed cycles (all at 37 °C, mixing and measuring as indicated).

steps.title: Export OCR data
steps.instruction: After the run (≈1 h), export point‑to‑point oxygen consumption rates (OCR) for each well from the Seahorse instrument.

steps.title: Quality‑control OCR traces
steps.instruction: Inspect each well’s oxygen‑tension trace; ensure the trace is linear during each measurement segment. Discard wells with non‑linear traces because they prevent reliable OCR calculation.

substeps.instruction: State 2: Max OCR at assay start – minimal OCR after antimycin A.
State 3: Max OCR after ADP injection – minimal OCR after antimycin A.
State 4o: Minimal OCR after oligomycin injection – minimal OCR after antimycin A (functionally equivalent to State 2).
Maximal: Max OCR after FCCP injection – minimal OCR after antimycin A.

description: Timing: 4 h1.Prepare batches of the Mitochondrial Isolation Buffer (MIB), Mitochondrial Assay Solution (MAS) and respirometry substrates solutions. The use of batch preparations reduces variability across independent isolations. Storage at −20°C of these buffers in single-use aliquots for 6 months is recommended, as freeze-thawing cycles can damage respirometry substrates. For MAS + GDP without substrates, single-use aliquots of 20 mL will provide sufficient buffer for the 96 wells in a plate/assay. For buffers containing 10× respirometry substrates with and without ADP, single-use aliquots of 1.5 and 2 mL respectively will provide sufficient buffer for one 96-well plate/assay. Refer to Materials and equipment tables for more details about the buffers that are stored at −20°C and buffers that are prepared on the day of the assay.CRITICAL: Adding respirometry substrates, such as pyruvate and malate, will acidify the MAS. Thus, the pH needs to be adjusted to pH 7.2 after adding substrates: pH ≤ 6 inhibits mitochondrial respiration.2.MIB stocks should be prepared with and without BSA. BSA is needed to trap free fatty acids released during adipose tissue homogenization, which can uncouple and damage mitochondria. However, BSA will interfere with the protein quantification assay needed to determine the yield of isolated mitochondria. Thus, the buffer without BSA is only used for the final resuspension of the mitochondrial pellet (Figure 1).Figure 1Schematic representation of peridroplet mitochondria (PDMs) isolation procedureBrown adipose tissue (BAT) is dissected from mice and homogenized with glass-Teflon Dounce homogenizer.
